items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: When I look at your list of people that you’ve collaborated with... Dexter Gordon... Like with Dexter we had one rehearsal... So in the middle of the set... we were at the Tralf... ctx.x: That’s a good one. I’ve heard people say and write about free jazz, because you mentioned Albert Ayler — a lot of times it seems like why are these musicians so angry. And I once asked Rashied Ali about that and he said it was more about just a reflection of the times. I wonder if you have a thought about that?

Yeah I think anger is a misinterpretation. Like one time they asked Archie Shepp was he angry. This was back in the heyday when Archie was pretty big in the ‘60s. And he said, he said, “Why are musicians so — are you guys angry?” He said, “No we’re not angry, we’re enraged.” You know? We’re enraged about the conditions, about the history, about the way we’ve been treated, about — Dexter Gordon talks about, in his biography he talks about how when he was in the Army, right — a Lieutenant or maybe a Sergeant or a…
